concepts.preferred_label: Pelvic inflammatory disease due to Neisseria gonorrhoeae
concepts.why: The patient's presentation of right lower-quadrant abdominal pain and the finding of a cystic mass with purulent fluid, combined with a negative HIV test, suggests a possible sexually transmitted infection such as Neisseria gonorrhoeae.

rationales.F01: Nausea, vomiting, and right lower-quadrant abdominal pain are non-specific symptoms that could be related to various conditions.
rationales.F03: The absence of fever makes some infectious conditions less likely.
rationales.F04: Tenderness in the right lower abdominal quadrant is a common finding in several conditions, including ovarian cyst infection and appendicitis.
rationales.F06: An elevated leukocyte count suggests an infectious or inflammatory process.
rationales.F07: An elevated C-reactive protein level indicates inflammation.
rationales.F08: A negative urine human chorionic gonadotropin test rules out ectopic pregnancy.
rationales.F10: The ultrasound suggesting retrocecal appendicitis was later found to be incorrect, as the appendix appeared normal during surgery.
rationales.F11: The discovery of a large cystic mass with regular margins arising from the right tubo-ovarian complex is highly suggestive of an ovarian cyst or tumor.
rationales.F12: The presence of purulent fluid within the cyst indicates infection.

frontier_selector.why: The presence of a 15 × 6 cm cystic mass with regular margins and purulent fluid noted upon incision of the cyst wall strongly supports the diagnosis of Tubo-ovarian abscess.
